draft.title: Human remains as evidence
card: In the 1980s and 1990s, archaeologists found hundreds of skeletons in the boat sheds at Herculaneum's shoreline. People had sheltered there from the eruption and were killed by the surge of hot gas and ash.
Bones and teeth record a person's life. Age at death, height, injuries and signs of disease can be read from them.
Chemical tests on bones and teeth show what a person ate. They can also show whether the person was exposed to substances such as lead.
Together, the skeletons give evidence about the health, diet and ages of ordinary people. Written sources rarely say much about this.
draft.remember: Skeletons from the boat sheds show how ordinary people lived, not only how they died.

a.q: Why are the skeletons from Herculaneum's boat sheds useful to historians?
opts: They give direct evidence of the victims' health and diet
They name the victims and record their jobs and families
They show exactly how many people lived in Herculaneum
They prove that nobody escaped from the eruption
a.why: Bones and teeth carry traces of illness, injury and food, so they tell us about how people lived. Skeletons do not name anyone and do not give a total population. The remains of those who died cannot show whether others escaped.
a.clue: Think about what bones and teeth record over a lifetime.

b.q: An archaeologist studies a skeleton from the boat sheds and finds a healed broken arm, worn teeth and a chemical trace of a diet rich in fish. What does this evidence best show?
opts: Details of this person's health and diet before the eruption
The exact cause of the eruption that killed this person
The name and social rank of the person who died
The route the person took to reach the boat sheds
b.why: A healed break, worn teeth and chemical traces all formed during the person's life, so they show health and diet. They say nothing about the eruption's cause. They also do not give a name or rank, and they do not show the route taken.
b.clue: Healed bones and chemical traces build up during life.

a.best: They give direct evidence of the victims' health and diet

b.best: Details of this person's health and diet before the eruption
